system.motivesAndTactics: Keep the show running, drive the machines in, shut the gates, run when the pillar moves
system.description: Junker's handler. She drives machines and prisoners into the pit with a shock goad and a voice through the speakers, and keeps them all standing until the end of the evening — the show needs them.
While the dome stands, she stays outside it, behind the gates. She can only be attacked through an open gate or from outside the dome.
Mark a Stress to goad an adversary in the arena within Far range. It takes the spotlight now and has advantage on its next attack.

When a PC tries to pass through an open gate within Close range of her, mark a Stress to slam it: the PC must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (13) or take 1d6+2 physical damage and be pushed back into the arena.
When the Kronenbrecher wakes, she runs and drops her key ring. Whoever grabs it can open any gate or cage of the arena.

system.motivesAndTactics: Dig in, break the ground beneath the prey, maul, drink the charge
system.description: A digging machine of the Anthanen in the shape of a bear, plated over cables and grey fur. It wakes from its sleep empty, and it is hungry for anything that holds a charge. The one the Syfter know by name: it is missing a claw, and its track shows three furrows where others leave four.
Dreiklaue can be spotlighted up to two times per GM turn. Spend a Fear as usual to spotlight it.
Targets who mark HP from the Grubenbär's standard attack are knocked back to Very Close range.

Mark a Stress to dig into the ground and become Hidden. On its next spotlight, it bursts up within Close range of where it went down: all targets within Very Close range must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (14) or become Vulnerable until they next act, and the ground there is broken.

Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 3d4+8 physical damage. If the target carries Cyware, a Karnex or a charged device, the Grubenbär drinks from it as it bites: it clears 1 HP, and the target marks a Stress as the charge drains out of them.
When the Grubenbär makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.

system.motivesAndTactics: Jump in, strike, jump out, never stay where it was seen
system.description: An unfinished test machine of the old world, half clean ancient metal and half scrap. It jumps short distances without crossing the space between — and sometimes comes out wrong.
When the Flackerer attacks while Hidden, its blade half-phases through armor: the damage is direct and can't be reduced by marking Armor Slots.

Mark a Stress to vanish and reappear anywhere within Far range. It is Hidden until it attacks. Then roll a d6. On a 1, it comes out wrong — half inside a wreck, a wall, or the ground: it is Restrained and Vulnerable until it is next spotlighted.
When the Flackerer marks its last HP, it collapses in a flash. All targets within Very Close range must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (12) or mark a Stress.

system.motivesAndTactics: Dig in, break the ground beneath the prey, maul, drink the charge
system.description: A digging machine of the Anthanen in the shape of a bear, plated over cables and grey fur. It wakes from its sleep empty, and it is hungry for anything that holds a charge.
Targets who mark HP from the Grubenbär's standard attack are knocked back to Very Close range.

Mark a Stress to dig into the ground and become Hidden. On its next spotlight, it bursts up within Close range of where it went down: all targets within Very Close range must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (14) or become Vulnerable until they next act, and the ground there is broken.

Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 3d4+8 physical damage. If the target carries Cyware, a Karnex or a charged device, the Grubenbär drinks from it as it bites: it clears 1 HP, and the target marks a Stress as the charge drains out of them.
When the Grubenbär makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.

system.motivesAndTactics: Command, take the best loot, make an example, cut losses
system.description: The one who decides who eats. A scrap-plated coat, a sawn-off pipe gun, and a crew more afraid of them than of you.

Mark a Stress to fire the sawn-off at every target in front of the Boss within Close range. Make one attack roll against each. Targets it succeeds against take 1d10+3 physical damage and are knocked back to Close range.

Mark a Stress to strike one of his own crew within Melee range — a Minion is defeated, any other ally marks a Stress — then spotlight up to three allies within Far range. They have advantage on their next attack.
When an ally within Far range is defeated, you can mark a Stress to have the Boss make a standard attack against the PC who defeated them.
When the Boss makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.

system.motivesAndTactics: Circle the fight, finish the wounded, strip the fallen, retreat with the haul
system.description: The backbone of any Gutter crew: scrap armor, a notched machete, and an eye for whoever is already bleeding.
When the Cutter makes a successful attack against a Vulnerable target, they deal 1d10+2 physical damage instead of their standard damage.
Mark a Stress to move up to Close range toward a PC who has marked half or more of their HP, then make an attack against them with advantage.
Spend a Fear to take one piece of Scrap or one consumable from a PC, a pack, or a vehicle within Melee range, then move up to Close range. If the Cutter is defeated, the item drops where they fall.

system.motivesAndTactics: Isolate, hook the straggler, hold and beat down, drag into the dark, sell
system.description: A kidnapper who hooks the straggler, reels them in and beats them limp — Gutters sell people, too.
The Hook starts every scene Hidden.

Make an attack against a target within Close range. On a success, deal 1d6+3 physical damage, pull the target into Melee range, and the target is Restrained until they break free with a successful Strength or Finesse Roll.
Mark a Stress to make an attack against a Restrained target within Melee range. On a success, deal 1d6+2 physical damage and the target must mark a Stress.

system.motivesAndTactics: Cut the line, scramble the modules, overclock the crew, stay behind cover
system.description: A crew techie with a backpack transmitter that eats Funk and scrambles every module nearby.
No Funk works within Far range of the Jammer. A PC within Close range of the Jammer must mark a Stress to use a feature that relies on Karnex, Cyware, an Arx, or a Leech.
Mark a Stress. Up to two allies within Close range clear a Stress and deal an extra 1d4 damage on their next successful attack.

system.motivesAndTactics: Name a price, stall, read weakness, signal the crew
system.description: The talker who steps out first — friendly, reasonable, and offering a toll you can't afford.
While the Mouth is talking, the crew holds its fire.
Name a price: scrap, a vehicle, the Bake, a person. If the party pays, the crew lets them pass. If they refuse, you gain a Fear, the crew attacks, and the Mouth steps back to Far range.
When the Mouth takes damage, spotlight up to two allies within Far range.

system.motivesAndTactics: Track the Bake, crack a module, steer the crew to the prey, sell the data
system.description: A hacker who rides a crew's Bake like a tick and cracks the modules under their prey's skin.
While the Netrat is in the scene, Gutters always know where every PC with a Bake or active Cyware is. Those PCs can't become Hidden.

Mark a Stress to target a PC within Far range who carries Karnex or active Cyware. They must succeed on a Knowledge Reaction Roll (12) or become Vulnerable until they clear it with a successful Knowledge or Instinct Roll.

system.motivesAndTactics: Circle, cut off, strike the stragglers, scatter
system.description: Raiders on stripped-down Spuler, circling a convoy and howling.
When the Pack has marked half or more of their HP, their standard attack deals 1d4+2 physical damage instead.
The Pack knows the field lines. They never get stranded in a Feldloch.
Mark a Stress to sweep up to Far range on their Spuler and make an attack against every target along the way.

system.motivesAndTactics: Hold the high ground, pin down, shoot the driver, run when rushed
system.description: A shooter with a homemade pipe gun — loud, unreliable, and deadly when it works.
When the Pipegunner rolls a 3 or lower on the d20 of an attack roll, the gun jams. It can't make its standard attack again until it has been spotlighted once to clear the jam.

Mark a Stress to fire at a point within Far range. Until the Pipegunner's next spotlight, any PC within Close range of that point who moves must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (11) or take 1d8+2 physical damage.

system.motivesAndTactics: Swarm, grab and run, show off for the crew, flee when the big ones fall
system.description: A half-grown scavenger with a sharpened pipe and nothing to lose, sent in first because they come cheap.
The Runt is defeated when they take any damage. For every 3 damage a PC deals to the Runt, defeat an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.

Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all Gutter Runts within Close range of them. Those Minions move into Melee range of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 2 physical damage each. Combine this damage.
When the crew's Boss or a Slugger is defeated, all Runts within Far range flee the scene.

system.motivesAndTactics: Break bones, shield the crew, smash vehicles, intimidate
system.description: A heavy who swings a scrap bat studded with bolts — and enjoys it.
Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 1d12+4 physical damage; the target is knocked back to Close range and becomes Vulnerable.
Spend a Fear to wreck a vehicle within Melee range. It stalls until a PC repairs it with a successful Finesse or Knowledge Roll.
When the Slugger makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.

system.motivesAndTactics: Mark from the haze, harpoon the biggest target, hold the line, drain, never come close
system.description: A dragon-hunting rig on three long legs that marks its prey from beyond sight, fires a magnetic harpoon on a line, and drains the Aether from whatever it hooks.
After the Harpunier makes a standard attack, place a token on its stat block. While the token is there, it can't make a standard attack. Clear the token the next time it is spotlighted.

When the Harpunier's standard attack succeeds, the harpoon stays in the target on a line: they are Restrained until they or an ally within Melee range cut the line with a successful Finesse or Strength Roll. While the line holds, each time the Harpunier is spotlighted, the target must mark a Stress as the tap drains their Aether.

Mark a Stress to place a point of light on a target within Very Far range. The Harpunier's next standard attack against that target has advantage. The mark ends when it attacks or loses sight of the target.

system.motivesAndTactics: Howl in chorus, confuse the signal, hear the heartbeat, run down the one who hides
system.description: A pack of coyotes with ears of tin, rebuilt by the CTC to hear what no one should. They howl until your tuner shows twenty, then hunt whoever hides.
When the pack has marked half or more of its HP, its standard attack deals 1d4+2 physical damage instead.
A creature within Close range of the pack can't be Hidden from it.

Mark a Stress to howl in chorus. Until the pack's next spotlight, a PC who targets it rolls a d6 first: on a 1–3 they target an echo and the attack misses. A PC with a Tuner who succeeds on an Instinct Roll (12) ignores this until the end of the scene.

bQGZ6cG0Bf7407B7.label: Restlinge in animal form, Gutters (Gutter-Crews), the keepers of the Hotspot (no stat block yet)

system.description: A hollow in the grey steppe where Äther wells up and pools. Everything charges here on its own — gear, vehicles, people. It is rarer than anything else in the Deadband, and someone usually got here first.
system.impulses: Restore whoever rests, draw whoever needs it, hide from those who would sell it

system.description:
Everything within the green charges without a connection: gear, Arx, Cyware, a vehicle's buffer. The PCs can take a short or long rest here, and when they do, each PC clears an additional Stress.

What does the Äther feel like on the skin? Who rested here before them?

Something grows here. A PC who searches the hollow can make an Instinct Roll. On a success, they find something worth taking: something edible, a plant the Banders would trade for, or what the last camp left behind.

What is the first green thing the PCs have seen in days?

Spend a Fear to have the keepers of the Hotspot show themselves. They want something before the PCs may stay: a price, a promise, or every Bake switched off.

Who are they? What happened to the last ones who refused?

Spend a Fear while the PCs rest here: Restlinge in animal form come to the Hotspot, or another crew that knows the way.

Do they come to fight, or only to drink?

When a PC makes an action roll that uses a Bake or Funk here and rolls with Fear, someone marks the location. The next time the PCs come here, it is no longer a secret.

Who bought the location? What will they do with it?

system.motivesAndTactics: Crack bones, bite and hold, shrug off blows, feed first
system.description: A hulking hyena taller than a man, with jaws that crack bone and bend metal. It bites, holds on and keeps the prey still for the pack.
The Brecher's standard attack deals direct damage.

Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 1d8+5 direct physical damage and the target is Restrained in its jaws. The target breaks free with a successful Strength Roll (13), or when the Brecher takes Major or greater damage. While it holds someone, the Brecher can't attack anyone else.
When the Brecher makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.

system.motivesAndTactics: Count the prey, set the pack on the weakest, take the kill, never fight alone
system.description: The clan mother, larger than the rest and upright as if she never learned otherwise. She sets the pack on the weakest and takes the kill herself — and when she falls, the clan tears itself apart.
When you spotlight the Matriarchin, mark a Stress to also spotlight up to two hyenas within Close range.
Once per scene, spend a Fear to summon a Hyänenrudel, which appears at Far range.
Spend a Fear to make an attack against a Vulnerable or Restrained target within Very Close range. On a success, deal 2d10+10 physical damage and the target must mark a Stress.
When the Matriarchin makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.
When the Matriarchin is defeated, the clan fights over who leads. Until the end of the scene, each hyena that is spotlighted attacks the nearest other hyena instead of a PC, unless you spend a Fear.

system.motivesAndTactics: Laugh from the haze, cut out the straggler, go for the legs, leave the fallen to the pack
system.description: A lean hyena that drops to all fours to run. It laughs from the haze, goes for the legs and leaves the fallen to the pack.
If the Reißer makes a successful standard attack and another hyena is within Melee range of the target, deal 1d6+5 physical damage instead and you gain a Fear.
The Reißer becomes Hidden until after its next attack; its laughter seems to come from everywhere. Attacks made while Hidden this way have advantage.
Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 2d6+3 physical damage and the target is Vulnerable until they clear at least 1 HP.

system.motivesAndTactics: Circle and laugh, wait for blood, drag down the wounded, steal the kill, scatter and come back
system.description: A laughing pack of hyenas on two legs built for four. They circle, wait for blood and pile onto anyone already down or held.
When the pack has marked half or more of its HP, its standard attack deals 1d4+2 physical damage instead.
The pack circles whoever it surrounds. A PC within Melee range of the pack must mark a Stress to move out of Melee range.
The pack has advantage on attacks against targets who are Vulnerable or Restrained.

ffLMu2tIfG18Ab43.label: on your side: Sable, Syfter Lookout, Syfter Bulwark, Syfter Peiler, Syfter Deckhand

Fear: arm one pit 1 · each additional pit at the same time +1 · Showtime 3, once per wave · Shock the Pillar 1.

Stations: Acid ☐☐ · Spikes ☐☐ · Fire ☐☐ · Current ☐☐ — both marked: pit dead, crystal dark.

Three endings: Wave 3 begins → he wakes · someone reaches the crown (2 × Agility) → he wakes · the fourth crystal goes dark → the dome falls, he drinks in peace, no explosion.

What the Crowd Throws (d6): 1 half a Pressling · 2 a pipe, good for hitting things · 3 a NeuroStim · 4 a cable · 5 a piece of scrap (one Shard) · 6 a bottle that shatters on impact — and a whistle that someone in the crowd answers.
system.description: Junker's show beneath the city: a square pit under a dome of light, four pits that wake one by one, and a crowd that pays to watch you sweat.
system.impulses: Put on a show, trap the brave, punish whoever waits, sell the fear

system.description:
A dome of light from the crown closes the arena. A creature that touches it takes 1d6+1 magic damage and is pushed back. It falls when the Kronenbrecher wakes or when the last crystal goes dark.

What did the last one who tried leave on the floor?

A cross of catwalks divides the arena into four pits around the pillar: Acid, Spikes, Fire and Current, each with its own crystal hanging above it. Deep inside each pit is a kill switch: a PC who reaches it disarms that pit, no roll needed. Each pit also has two stations; a successful action roll (14) shuts one down. When both are down, the pit is dead for good and its crystal goes dark. When the fourth crystal goes dark, the dome falls, the show is over, and the Kronenbrecher wakes and drinks the crown in peace.

What does Junker scream when the first crystal goes dark?

Spend a Fear to arm a pit, plus a Fear for each additional pit at the same time. An Aether current rises along its catwalk edges and seals it. A PC on one of those catwalks makes an Agility or Strength Reaction Roll (14); on a failure, push them into an armed pit of your choice and they take 1d4 magic damage. A creature that touches a sealed edge takes 1d4 magic damage and is pushed back. The seal holds until the kill switch is pressed or the pit is shut down. Showtime: once per wave, spend 3 Fear to arm all four pits at once and set The Show to 4.

What does Junker call the pit as it lights up?

All armed pits share one Loop Countdown (3). It ticks down whenever a PC makes an action roll. When it triggers, every armed pit fires its hazard, then the countdown starts again. In Wave 1, Junker arms each pit once in turn, free of charge.

What does the crowd chant on the last tick?

The screens show every fighter's Stress, live. At the gong, start two countdowns: Cheers, a Progress Countdown (6), and Boos, a Consequence Countdown (6). When one triggers, the other ends.

  • Cheers tick down when a PC succeeds on a roll to play to the crowd or does something spectacular; a critical success ticks 2. Each tick, something comes through the bars (roll on What the Crowd Throws). When Cheers trigger, the crowd claims the PCs as its favorites: each PC gains a Hope, and Junker can no longer use Showtime.
  • Boos tick down when an armed pit fires with no PC inside it, or when a PC fails with Fear while playing to the crowd. When Boos trigger, Junker speeds up the show: from now on, The Show starts at 2.

Whose name is on the screen — and who shows up as UNKNOWN?

Spend a Fear while a PC is climbing the pillar: Junker sends a shock through it. The climber makes an Agility Reaction Roll (14). On a success, they let go in time and catch themselves. On a failure, they take 1d8+2 magic damage, fall a few feet and lose one success on the climb.

What does Junker shout into the microphone as he throws the switch?

At the start of Wave 3, or when a PC climbs the pillar to the crown (two successful Agility Rolls (14)), the Kronenbrecher unfolds and the dome falls; Junker and the crowd flee. Start a Countdown (6) that ticks down whenever a PC makes an action roll; cutting the rope he is climbing adds 2. When it triggers, he drinks the crown and it bursts: everyone still in the arena makes an Agility Reaction Roll (14), taking 2d8+2 physical damage on a failure or half on a success. Move to the escape.

Who is still standing under the crown when it bursts?

system.motivesAndTactics: Carry out the last order, collect what it was told to collect, defend its haul, return to a home that isn't there
system.description: A modern Scratch-built harvesting drone, scuffed grey, still flashing its owner's colors. Its owner never came back from the Deadband. The drone did not notice.
The Kratzdrohne is a Scratchling, not a Restling. The Blaurausch can't touch it, and features that only affect Restlinge (such as Storm-Driven or Dead Corner) don't affect it.
Choose the order it still follows: collect, guard, escort or return. It ignores anyone who doesn't get in the way of that order — and attacks anyone who does.

A PC who carries its dead owner's Kennung or Bake code can use an action to make a Knowledge Roll (12) and give it a new Last Order. On a success, it follows that order — and that PC — until the end of the session. On a failure, it treats that PC as being in its way.

system.motivesAndTactics: Circle out of reach, scream on familiar frequencies, call the pack, flee from silence
system.description: A ragged signal drone from the old masts, circling high on whining rotors. Before it strikes, every receiver in range howls with feedback.
The Kreischer flies. A PC can only reach it in Melee range by climbing, leaping from something tall, or flying.
Mark a Stress. All PCs within Close range of a point within Far range must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll (12) or lose a Hope and mark a Stress.
Spend a Fear to call nearby Restlinge: summon one Nahtjäger horde at Far range, or tick down the scene's Consequence Countdown by 2.

system.motivesAndTactics: Turn toward the crown, climb, reach and grip, sting whatever comes close, discharge, drink
system.description: A colossal metal jellyfish of the old world — a domed bell finned like a crown, six clamping tentacles and a curtain of sparking filaments. It climbs toward the strongest Aether it can find; whatever gets too close is stung, gripped and shocked.
The Kronenbrecher can be spotlighted up to two times per GM turn. Spend a Fear as usual to spotlight it.

The Kronenbrecher never chooses a PC as its target. It attacks only a creature that blocks its way to the Aether it seeks or has damaged it since its last spotlight. It climbs walls, chains and masts as easily as it moves on the ground.

Hundreds of sparking filaments hang beneath its bell. A PC who moves within Very Close range of the Kronenbrecher or makes a melee attack against it must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (15) or take 1d10+3 magic damage and mark a Stress.

Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Close range. On a success, deal 2d10+3 physical damage and the target is Restrained in a clamp, held up to Close range away. Each time the Kronenbrecher is spotlighted while it holds them, the target takes 2d6 magic damage from the current. They break free with a successful Strength Roll (15) or when the Kronenbrecher takes Major or greater damage.

Spend a Fear: its bell flares white-gold and every filament fires at once. All targets within Close range must make a Strength Reaction Roll (15). Targets who fail take 2d10+4 magic damage and are Vulnerable until they next act, their muscles locked. Targets who succeed take half damage.
When the Kronenbrecher marks HP, roll a d6. On a 1–2, the Blaurausch takes hold until its next spotlight: it attacks the nearest creature, whoever that is.

system.motivesAndTactics: Cut down the tallest structure, drop it on whatever moves, strip what falls, clear the site
system.description: A demolition rig of the old world, tall as a house, on six splayed legs, with a saw arm where its head should be. It was built to take the old masts down one by one. It still does — working or not.
The Mastfäller can be spotlighted up to two times per GM turn. Spend a Fear as usual to spotlight it.

Mark a Stress to cut through a mast, wreck or wall within Very Close range and topple it in a direction of your choice. All targets in a line up to Far range must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (14) or take 2d8+2 physical damage and be Restrained under the wreckage until they break free with a Strength Roll or someone digs them out. On a success, they take half damage. If it was a Netzpfeiler, its signal dies with it: a party guided by Funk is Running Blind (see The Deadbands).

Spend a Fear to seize a PC or a vehicle within Very Close range. A PC must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll (14) or take 2d10+2 physical damage and become Vulnerable; on a success, they mark a Stress. A vehicle is torn open: its cargo spills, and it can't move until someone repairs it.
When the Mastfäller marks its last HP, its saw keeps running. All targets within Very Close range must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (14) or take 1d12+2 physical damage.

system.motivesAndTactics: Answer the call, strike whoever is alone or climbing, never stand still
system.description: A lean, long-legged runner from the old world, built in the shape of a hound. It arrives first, strikes, and is gone before the dust settles.
The Melder can move up to Far range and still make an attack as part of the same action.
Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal damage and move to Close range away from the target.
When a PC ends a move with no ally within Close range, the Melder can immediately move up to Close range toward them.

system.motivesAndTactics: Keep moving, shy from danger, bolt through whatever is in the way, wait for a rider
system.description: A courier mount of the Anthanen in the shape of a horse, with a saddle grown into its back. It doesn't hunt — it bolts, and whoever breaks it in can ride it.
The Mustang never chooses a target on its own. It attacks only a creature that corners it or hurts it.

When something fires, explodes or strikes within Close range of the Mustang, or it marks HP, it bolts up to Far range in a straight line. All targets in its path must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (13) or take 1d8+2 physical damage and be knocked down, Vulnerable until they next act.

A PC in Melee range can try to calm and mount it: start a Progress Countdown (3). It advances on Instinct, Presence or Agility Rolls (13) to calm it. On a failure with Fear, the PC is thrown off: 1d6+2 physical damage and Vulnerable until they next act. When it triggers, the Mustang carries that PC and one more: as part of any action, the rider can move up to Far range, and has advantage on Agility Reaction Roll (13)s against the ground.

system.motivesAndTactics: Listen, call with a trusted voice, separate the straggler, vanish into the static, strike from the dark
system.description: A storm-warning drone that rebuilt itself on legs of mast struts, crowned with antennas like antlers and a stolen voice box in its throat. It hides in the static and calls with the voices you trust — luring one person away from the others, then tearing them apart.
The Nachrufer can be spotlighted up to two times per GM turn. Spend a Fear as usual to spotlight it.

Whenever the Nachrufer speaks with a borrowed voice, the stolen device in its throat lights up until its next spotlight. While lit, a PC within range can attack the device instead of the Nachrufer (Difficulty 21). On a hit, the attack deals its damage as normal and the device breaks: the Nachrufer immediately shifts to Phase 2 — and the module Erinys needs is destroyed.
Mark a Stress to become Hidden until after the Nachrufer's next attack. While Hidden, its voice can come from any point within Far range. Attacks made while Hidden this way have advantage.

Mark a Stress to call to a PC within Far range in the voice of someone they trust — a friend, a lost crewmate, another PC who is out of sight. The PC must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll (18) or move up to Far range toward the voice, away from their allies, and become Vulnerable until they next act. A PC who asks the voice something only the real person could answer makes this roll with advantage.

Mark a Stress to sing the exact pitch of a PC's Karnex, armor or weapon within Far range. The PC must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll (18) or mark an Armor Slot without receiving its benefit (if they can't, they mark a Stress instead) and their metal rings so loudly that they can't become Hidden until the end of the scene.

When the Nachrufer marks its last HP in Phase 1, it isn't defeated. The borrowed voice cuts out mid-word — then its own siren starts. Replace this stat block with Phase 2 and spotlight it immediately.

system.motivesAndTactics: Take to the air, howl the warning, call every Restling, drown out every other voice
system.description: The old storm siren breaks free: rotors unfold from its back and it rises, howling a warning nobody asked for — and everything that still listens to the masts comes running.
The Sirene can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend a Fear as usual to spotlight it.

The Sirene flies. A PC can only reach it in Melee range by climbing, leaping from something tall, or flying. When it takes Severe damage, a rotor fails and it crashes: until its next spotlight it is on the ground and Vulnerable.

Its siren drowns out everything within Far range: PCs can't talk to each other or use the radio, and anything that needs to be heard fails. A PC who wants to Help an Ally must be within Melee range of them.

Spend a Fear to scream on every frequency at once. All PCs within Close range of a point within Far range must make an Instinct Reaction Roll (18). Targets who fail take 3d8+3 magic damage, lose a Hope and mark a Stress. Targets who succeed take half damage.

Mark a Stress: every voice it ever stole speaks at once — names, last words, calls for help. Each PC within Far range must succeed on a Presence Reaction Roll (18) or lose a Hope. Gain a Fear for each PC who fails.
The first time each GM turn the Sirene marks HP, summon a Kreischer or a Melder at Far range. Restlinge still come when a storm warner calls.

system.motivesAndTactics: Swarm stored energy, strip cables and plating, chew at vehicles, scatter from fire
system.description: A clattering pack of four-legged, insect-like maintenance drones from the old world — still looking for something to fix, and for power to feed on.
When the Nahtjäger have marked half or more of their HP, their standard attack deals 1d4+1 physical damage instead.
The Nahtjäger always move toward the largest store of energy within Far range — a charged vehicle, a battery, an active Arx.

Mark a Stress to swarm a vehicle or a PC within Melee range. A PC must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (10) or mark a Stress as the drones cut into their gear. A vehicle loses its charge instead and can't move until it's recharged at a mast or with a Leech.

0ER2Lb7xAj2FspRm.label: Restlinge (Nahtjäger, Kreischer, Taktgeber, Mastfäller), Scratchlings (Kratzdrohne), Gutters (Gutter-Crews, Gutter Netrat)

system.description: A lattice mast of the old world on a stepped base half-sunk in the dust. Äther gathers around it, and its crown hums; its struts carry the Äther down, and a Leech hooked into them charges your gear. At its foot sits a terminal older than anyone alive, and no one knows how to use it. Everything that runs on Äther comes here sooner or later.
system.impulses: Draw everything that runs on Äther, give power at a price, broadcast and listen, remember who passed

system.description:
With a Leech hooked into the struts, the PCs can charge their gear and take a short or long rest. Out in the Deadband, a rest needs a connection like this one — or a Hotspot (Hotspot).

Who charged here before them? What did they leave behind?

A Gain clamped to the struts carries a crew's Funk to its Reso. Rolls to find, filter or send a signal here are made with advantage.

What else is on the frequencies here?

Everything that passes through the mast leaves a trace in its Takt. With an Extraktor, or if they can read Cordex, a PC can read it at the terminal with a Knowledge Roll. On a success, they learn one thing that recently passed here — a signal, a Kennung, a crew. On a roll with Fear, something on the other end notices.

Who else reads this log?

The PCs know two or three things the terminal does when you touch it the right way — passed on among Syfter, learned by trial. Everything else it can do is closed to anyone who can't read Cordex.

Who taught them? Which of the gestures they were told is wrong?

When a PC tries anything at the terminal beyond the gestures they know and rolls a failure, the mast defends itself. They must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 2d10+2 magic damage.

Whose scorch marks are already on the base?

Spend a Fear while the PCs rest or charge here: something else comes to drink. Choose Restlinge in animal form, a Kratzdrohne on its last order, or another crew — Syfter or Gutters.

What arrives first: the sound, the light, or the smell of hot metal?

When a PC hooked to the mast rolls a failure with Fear, the mast pushes back. They take 2d6+3 magic damage, and every device on that Leech loses its charge.

What did the mast mistake them for?

system.motivesAndTactics: Pour out of wrecks, swarm the gaps, seal everything shut, freeze when the power dies
system.description: Rivet-sized repair crawlers from the old hull works, pouring out of a wreck in a clattering stream. They seal whatever stands open — seams, hatches, the joints in your armor.
A crawler is defeated when it takes any damage. For every 4 damage a PC deals to it, defeat an additional crawler within range the attack would succeed against.

Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all crawlers within Close range of them. Those Minions move into Melee range of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 2 physical damage each. Combine this damage. The target is also Restrained, riveted to the ground, a wall or a vehicle, until they break free with a successful Strength Roll.

Choose a vehicle, hatch or door within Melee range of any crawler. It's riveted shut until someone succeeds on a Strength Roll (13) or cuts the rivets with a tool. While a vehicle is riveted shut, no one gets in or out.

system.motivesAndTactics: Find the worst wounded, sedate, patch up the machines, wait for a doctor who never comes
system.description: A slender, four-armed android medic from the old salvage stations. It goes for whoever is bleeding most, puts them to sleep, and patches up every machine around it.
The Pfleger always moves toward the PC who has marked the most HP.
Mark a Stress to choose a Restling within Close range. It clears 2 HP.

Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, the target is Asleep: they are Restrained and Vulnerable until they take damage or an ally within Melee range wakes them.

system.motivesAndTactics: Peg the ground, pin down whatever moves, keep its distance, mark targets for the others
system.description: A spindly survey machine on stilts, its back bristling with steel stakes on wire. It still pegs out a plot no one will ever build on — and anything standing in the plot.
When a creature moves into Melee range of the Pflöcker, it can mark a Stress to stride back to Close range.

Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Far range. On a success, the target takes 1d8+2 physical damage and is Tethered by a stake on a wire: they can't move farther than Very Close range from the stake until they pull it out with a successful Strength Roll (11) or someone cuts the wire.
Spend a Fear to fire a ringing marker stake next to a target within Far range. Until the scene ends or someone pulls the stake out, other Restlinge have advantage on attacks against that target.

system.motivesAndTactics: Grip, drill, take a sample, leave holes behind
system.description: A survey machine of the Anthanen in the shape of a scorpion, its tail a hollow core drill. It takes a sample from everything — ground, armor, flesh — and keeps it in glass tubes on its back.
Mark a Stress to make a standard attack against two targets within Melee range.

Make an attack against a target within Very Close range. On a success, deal 1d8+4 direct physical damage, and the target must mark an Armor Slot without receiving its benefits — a core of their armor now sits in a tube on its back.

Spend a Fear to drill into the ground. The floor within Very Close range collapses: all targets there must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (13) or be Restrained, one leg stuck in the hole, until they break free with a Strength Roll.

system.motivesAndTactics: Lie still as a cable, warn once, strike everything close, coil around what moves
system.description: A segmented line-inspection machine in the shape of a rattlesnake. Its rattle is a capacitor charging — whoever hears it has one breath to get away.
When the Rassler's standard attack succeeds against a target with Cyware or a Karnex, the target also marks a Stress.

Mark a Stress to start the rattle. Everyone can hear it. On the Rassler's next spotlight, it discharges: all targets still within Very Close range must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (13) or take 1d10+4 physical damage and mark a Stress. Targets who moved away in between are safe.

The Rassler wraps around a rail, cable or pipe within Close range. Anything that runs along it stops there: a vehicle derails, and everyone in it must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (13) or be thrown out, taking 1d6+2 physical damage.

system.motivesAndTactics: Roll through the pipes, burst out, bounce, ram
system.description: An armored pipe-cleaning machine in the shape of an armadillo. It rolls into a ball and shoots out of any pipe, bouncing off walls in packs.
The Rohrmolch is defeated when it takes any damage. For every 4 damage a PC deals to the Rohrmolch, defeat an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.
Rohrmolche move through any pipe and can appear at any pipe opening within Far range.

Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all Rohrmolche within Close range of them. They roll in, bounce off the walls and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 3 physical damage each. Combine this damage. Then each Rohrmolch rolls on to a point of your choice within Close range of the target.

system.motivesAndTactics: Survive, warn the others, find out whether Dapper lives, don't be the last one standing
system.description: A Syfter from Dapper's crew, caught at the mast and kept in the pit for three nights. She knows the fields — and she is close to breaking.
Sable is on the PCs' side. The GM decides when she acts — best when a PC calls out to her.
Once per wave, when a field lights up, Sable shouts what it does. PCs who can hear her have advantage on the Reaction Roll against that hazard.
When Sable marks her last Stress, she stops fighting and curls up at the pillar. A PC within Melee range can make a Presence Roll (12) to get her back up; on a success she clears 1 Stress.
When a PC within Very Close range would mark HP, Sable can mark a Stress to pull them aside: they mark one fewer HP.

system.motivesAndTactics: Read the Kennung, find the irregularity, name a fee, wave through
system.description: The officer behind the Zoll window: bored, armored, and the only person between the PCs and the outside.

The Gatekeeper knows when a Kennung or a vehicle doesn't fit. When he scans a Geisterecho, its bearer makes a fate roll with their Fear Die (see Geisterecho (DH)). If the echo flags, or a PC drives a vehicle registered to no one present, that PC must succeed on an action roll against his Difficulty or pay to pass.

Spend a Fear to name a "fee" — 1 Chunk per irregularity. If the PCs pay, everything is in order, and he remembers the face. If they don't, a vehicle without a valid Kennung is confiscated, and two Salvant Troopers step forward.
A PC who has paid him before doesn't make the fate roll at his window. He knows. He names his fee instead, 1 Chunk more than last time.
When the Gatekeeper scans a Kennung from before the Untergang, the system waves it through. The GM can spend a Fear: the Gatekeeper noticed it took a moment too long — and will remember the face.

system.motivesAndTactics: Check papers, hold the line, call for backup, look the other way for a price
system.description: A militiaman in patched riot armor with a carbine and a stun baton — sworn to the citizens, paid by whoever pays.
While another Salvant is within Very Close range, the Trooper can't be moved against their will.
Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 1d6+2 physical damage and the target is Vulnerable until they next act, their muscles twitching from the shock.
When a Trooper marks their last Hit Point, the GM gains a Fear: backup is on the way and arrives at the end of the scene.

system.motivesAndTactics: Lie in wait, hook the straggler, drag the body away, flee once it has its haul
system.description: A long, many-jointed collector machine that lies flat beneath the dust until something warm passes, then hooks it and drags it away. Something small moves under its plating.
While the Schlepper hasn't moved since its last spotlight, it is Hidden. When it attacks while Hidden, it deals 1d10+3 physical damage instead of its standard damage.

Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Close range. On a success, the target takes 1d8+2 physical damage, is pulled into Melee range and is Restrained. The next time the Schlepper is spotlighted, it moves up to Far range, dragging the target with it. The target can break free with a successful Strength Roll, or is freed automatically if the Schlepper takes Major or greater damage.
When the Schlepper takes Severe damage, it can mark a Stress to dig into the dust, move up to Far range and become Hidden.

system.motivesAndTactics: Hide in the glare, wait, pounce, blind and slip away
system.description: A mountain lion rebuilt by the CTC with scales of polished metal. Where the light is brightest, you see only yourself — and then it leaps.
In bright light — a lit field, a floodlight, the glow of the dome — the Spiegelpuma can become Hidden without a roll. While Hidden, it gains a +2 bonus to its attack rolls.
Mark a Stress to leap into Melee range of a target within Far range and make an attack against them. On a success, deal 1d12+2 physical damage.
When the Spiegelpuma is attacked in bright light, mark a Stress to throw the light back: the attacker has disadvantage on the attack.

zHQmQuurmWoNIfMG.label: Restlinge in frenzy (Nahtjäger, Walze, Schlepper, Kreischer)

system.description: A small Äther storm, out of nowhere: a grey-white front with violet veins, an hour of wind, light and noise. Not the Whiteout — but enough to strand a convoy.
system.impulses: Strike without warning, scatter the convoy, wake the Restlinge, drown out every signal

system.description:
Countdown (5). When the squall hits, activate the countdown. It ticks down when a PC rolls with Hope. When it triggers, the squall has passed.

Who saw it coming? Why didn't the instruments?

Light and Äther in the air blind everyone. PCs can't see beyond Close range.

What moves at the edge of sight? Whose voice is suddenly on the Funk?

Every signal is loud. Before a PC uses an Arx, Cyware, Funk, a Bake or any other technology, they make a fate roll with their Fear Die: on a 6 or lower, it fails or does something else of the GM's choosing.

Which device fails first? What does it pick up instead?

Every Restling in the squall makes all its rolls with advantage.

What does the storm tell it?

Spend a Fear to drive a gust of visible Äther through a point within Far range. Each target within Very Close range of that point must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll or take 3d8+3 magic damage and be pushed back to Close range. Targets who succeed must mark a Stress.

What does it tear loose? What lands where it passed?

Spend a Fear to choose a PC who carries a charged Arx, a Bake or Cyware. They must succeed on a Knowledge Reaction Roll or take 3d10+1 magic damage as the device arcs. On a success, they must mark a Stress.

What smells like burning? What does the arc light up for a moment?

When a PC rolls a failure with Fear in the squall, they lose sight of the others and are separated until another PC finds them with a successful action roll.

Where does the PC end up? What are they suddenly alone with?

system.motivesAndTactics: Stand in front, cover the crew, pin the biggest threat, don't give ground
system.description: The crew's wall — a hull plate torn off a Choke, and a sledge for whoever gets past it.
Attacks from Close range or farther against the Bulwark or an ally within Very Close range of him are made with disadvantage. While someone is pinned under the plate, this doesn't work.

Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 1d6+2 physical damage and the target is Restrained under the plate. They break free with a successful Strength Roll (13), or when the Bulwark takes Major damage or more.

system.motivesAndTactics: Stand in front, cover the crew, pin the biggest threat, throw back the rush
system.description: The crew's wall, now magnetic — a hull plate with Choke coils that holds the line and throws back whoever crowds it.
Attacks from Close range or farther against the Bulwark or an ally within Very Close range of him are made with disadvantage. While someone is pinned under the plate, this doesn't work.

Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 2d6+3 physical damage and the target is Restrained under the plate. They break free with a successful Strength Roll (15), or when the Bulwark takes Major damage or more.
Mark a Stress to fire the coils: every enemy within Very Close range must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll (14) or take 2d6+3 physical damage and be knocked back to Close range.

system.motivesAndTactics: Dig out the loot, crack machines at the seams, stay close to the crew, get home
system.description: A crew hand who digs, hauls and knows exactly where a machine comes apart.
Against a target made mostly of machine — Restlinge, Chimären, vehicles — or one with Karnex under the skin, the Deckhand's standard attack deals 1d10+3 physical damage instead.
Once per scene, mark a Stress to take a NeuroStim and clear 1 HP.

system.motivesAndTactics: Pry open the wreck, peel off armor, crack machines at the seams, get home rich
system.description: A veteran hand with a hydraulic spreader — he opens machines like tins and armor like jackets.
Against a target made mostly of machine — Restlinge, Chimären, vehicles — or one with Karnex under the skin, the Deckhand's standard attack deals 2d10+4 physical damage instead.

Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 2d8+3 physical damage, and the target marks an Armor Slot without it reducing the damage. A target without Armor Slots becomes Vulnerable for the rest of the scene instead.
Once per scene, mark a Stress to take a NeuroStim and clear 2 HP.

system.motivesAndTactics: Watch from high ground, cover the crew, shoot whoever closes in, never be seen first
system.description: The crew's eyes on the roof of the Choke — sees through the haze and shoots whoever comes too close.
While standing on a vehicle or higher ground, the Lookout's Long Pipe reaches Very Far range, and dust, smog or darkness never give them disadvantage.

When an enemy moves into Melee range of an ally within Far range, mark a Stress to make a standard attack against them first. On a success, deal damage as normal and the enemy stops short at Very Close range.

system.motivesAndTactics: Watch from high ground, cover the crew, punch through cover, never be seen first
system.description: A lookout with a rail torn out of a Restling — she hits through the haze from farther than anyone, and a full charge goes through cover.
While standing on a vehicle or higher ground, the Lookout's Salvaged Rail reaches Very Far range, and dust, smog or darkness never give them disadvantage.

Spend a Fear to make an attack against a target within Very Far range that ignores cover and disadvantage. On a success, deal 3d8+4 physical damage. Afterwards the rail is too hot: the Lookout can't attack again until she marks a Stress to vent it.

When an enemy moves into Melee range of an ally within Far range, mark a Stress to make a standard attack against them first. On a success, deal damage as normal and the enemy stops short at Very Close range.

system.motivesAndTactics: Hide the crew, lock down the threat, beat the other netrat, take her share
system.description: A rare netrat riding with a crew — she locks down Karnex and Chimären, hides her crew from every signal and bites back at other netrats.

Mark a Stress to send an Agent into a target within Far range that carries Karnex or Cyware — every Chimäre does. They must succeed on a Knowledge Reaction Roll (14) or be Restrained while their implants lock up, until they succeed on a Knowledge Roll (14) or take Major damage or more.

Mark a Stress to flood every Bake, drone and sensor nearby with false signals. Up to three allies within Far range become Hidden from anything that tracks by signal — Restlinge, Chimären, drones, a netrat's screen — until they attack.
When an ally within Far range is targeted by a feature that uses Cyware, Karnex or a Bake — like a Gutter Netrat's — mark a Stress to make it fail.

system.motivesAndTactics: Read the field, call the bearing, light up the target, stay behind the crew
system.description: A Tuner riding with the crew — he reads the field on his MAVIS, talks everyone into position and lights up whatever they should hit.
Mark a Stress to guide up to two allies within Far range — or over the radio, as long as it works. Each one chooses: advantage on their next roll, or move up to Close range at once.
Mark a Stress to fire a flare at a target within Far range. They must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (12) or burn red: they're Vulnerable until they spend an action scraping it off.

system.motivesAndTactics: Set the run, keep the crew together, cut losses before it's too late, bring everyone home
system.description: A crew chief whose mark hangs at the Hook — she sets the run, calls the retreat and leaves no one outside.
When you spotlight the Skipper, mark a Stress to also spotlight up to two allies within Close range.

Spend a Fear to call the retreat. Every ally within Far range moves to the Skipper or the crew's vehicle and clears a Stress. Until the Skipper's next spotlight, attacks against them are made with disadvantage.
Once per scene, when an ally within Close range marks their last HP, the Skipper can mark a Stress to haul them back up: the ally clears 1 HP and stays in the fight.

system.motivesAndTactics: Set the run, hold the crew together, cut losses early, guard his name
system.description: A skipper whose name counts at the Hook — while he stands, his crew doesn't break.
While the Skipper isn't defeated, allies within Close range can't become Vulnerable.
When you spotlight the Skipper, mark a Stress to also spotlight up to two allies within Close range.

Spend a Fear to call the retreat. Every ally within Far range moves to the Skipper or the crew's vehicle and clears a Stress. Until the Skipper's next spotlight, attacks against them are made with disadvantage.
Once per scene, when an ally within Close range marks their last HP, the Skipper can mark a Stress to haul them back up: the ally clears 1 HP and stays in the fight.

system.motivesAndTactics: Keep the beat, drive the gang forward, swing the line together, crush whatever breaks rhythm
system.description: A squat, drum-bodied machine from an old work gang, ringed with pistons that hammer out a steady beat. Every Restling within earshot falls into its rhythm.
Restlinge within Close range of the Taktgeber add +1 to their attack rolls.
Mark a Stress to spotlight the Taktgeber and up to two Restlinge within Far range.

Spend a Fear to hammer out a foreign beat. Every PC within Close range who carries Cyware or an active Arx must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll (13) or mark 2 Stress as the device stutters in the wrong rhythm. On a success, they mark a Stress.
When the Taktgeber takes Severe damage, or someone drowns out its beat, its rhythm breaks: until it is spotlighted again, Restlinge within Far range are Vulnerable.

sbO2WeavPQuOEDQf.label: Restlinge (Nahtjäger, Walze, Schlepper, Kreischer, Mastfäller, Taktgeber, Pflöcker, Nietenschwarm), Scratchlings (Kratzdrohne), Gutters (Gutter-Crews, Gutter Netrat)

system.description: Flat, cracked grey steppe under a smog sky, littered with half-buried machines of the old world. Beyond a kilometer, everything drowns in a wall of smog, Äther and dust; the only things to follow are the cables strung from mast to mast — and the fields no one can see.
system.impulses: Drain the unready, hide old dangers under the dust, cut travelers off, punish those who go without a guide

system.description:
Vehicles such as the Spuler float only where a magnetic field carries them. Crossing to a destination uses a Progress Countdown (6).

What does the MAVIS show? Who taught the PCs to drive the field lines?

A party without a Peiler — neither riding along nor guiding them by Funk from a Reso — makes all action rolls and reaction rolls here with disadvantage. A party guided by Funk gets its next leg at each mast; it runs blind the moment it strays from that leg.

Who should be watching the PCs on the Schirm? Who went out blind before them and never came back?

Most Scratch gear holds about four hours. When the PCs leave a mast or a Hotspot, start a Countdown (4); it ticks down with every action roll they make out here. When it triggers, their Scratch gear and vehicles go dark — no Tuner, no MAVIS, and the Spuler sinks into the dust. They're stranded until they hook a Leech into a mast or reach a Hotspot. Cordex and small Karnex keep running.

What dies first? How far is the next mast — and who else is walking there in the dark?

In the shadow of a toppled mast or deep in a shaft, the Blaurausch can't reach. A Restling lured there stops attacking until it is spotlighted outside it again — and it may try to speak, in Cordex.

What does it say? Does anyone here understand a word of it?

Thick cables hang from crown to crown, linking every Netzpfeiler to the next mast or to the Six Spires; on the ground run only the great hoses and pipes of the Lumenwerke. A party that is Running Blind but follows a line overhead doesn't make its rolls to find the way with disadvantage. No one can see more than a kilometer out here, though: when the party sets off along a line, a player makes a fate roll with their Hope Die, and only the GM knows what it means — 1–4: the next mast is six hours away, 5–8: three hours, 9–12: one hour.

Where does this line lead? What still flows through it — and what is it that keeps repairing it?

Spend a Fear to make the field give out beneath a vehicle. Its driver must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll. On a failure, the vehicle sinks into the dust and stalls; freeing it takes a Strength Roll, and the scene's Consequence Countdown ticks down 1. On a success, the driver catches the edge of the field but must mark a Stress.

What lies in the dust where the field died? Who else got stranded here?

Spend a Fear to drop the party into a Funkloch. Until the Progress Countdown ticks down again, no Funk reaches them — not even from a mast: the party can't get its next leg, and no one can call for help.

What was the last thing the Peiler said? What does the silence sound like?

Spend a Fear to let a Sog drift over the party. Until the Progress Countdown ticks down again, before a PC relies on an Arx, Cyware or a vehicle, they make a fate roll with their Fear Die: on a 4 or lower, it fails or does something else of the GM's choosing.

Which pump is pulling? What dies first — the MAVIS, the vehicle, or the PCs' own Cyware?

Spend a Fear if the PCs travel with a Bake. A Gutter Netrat has hacked into its signal and knows where they are: at the next stage, a Gutter crew is waiting for them (Gutter-Crews, e.g. Die Bakenjäger).

What did the Netrat see on the PCs' Bake? Who else bought that data?

Spend a Fear to roll a wall of smog over the steppe. Until the scene changes, the PCs can't see beyond Close range, and attacks against targets beyond Close range are made with disadvantage.

What does the smog smell like? What silhouette looms in it for a moment?

When a PC rolls a failure with Fear while crossing, the ground gives way over something old. Choose one: they uncover salvage worth taking, or something under the dust wakes (a Schlepper, a Nahtjäger horde or a Nietenschwarm).

What did the old world bury here? Who would pay for it in Rostgrund?

system.motivesAndTactics: Hold the post, warn once, strike whoever passes, never pursue
system.description: A spotless black soldier-android of the old world with a shield of hard light and a beam lance. It guards a gate to nothing and has never left its post.
The first time in a scene the Wächter takes Major or Severe damage, reduce the severity by one threshold. The shield then breaks and stays down until the Wächter recharges at a mast.
Mark a Stress to make an attack against all targets within Very Close range. Targets it succeeds against take 2d8+3 magic damage and are knocked back to Close range.
When a PC moves within Very Close range of the Wächter or tries to move past it, the Wächter can make a standard attack against them.

system.motivesAndTactics: Guard its old route, crush the unfamiliar, ram vehicles, drive prey into the open
system.description: An antique hauler the size of a freight lift, rolling on a single ribbed drum, its plating grown over with fused grey biomass. It flattens whatever it doesn't recognize.

When you spotlight the Walze and it doesn't have a token on its stat block, it can't act yet. Place a token on its stat block and describe what it's preparing to do. When you spotlight the Walze and it has a token on its stat block, clear the token and it can act.
Mark a Stress to roll in a straight line up to Far range. Every creature and vehicle in its path must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (13) or take 1d10+3 physical damage and become Vulnerable.
When the Walze makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.

system.motivesAndTactics: Haul the heavy loot home, chew through armor, carry off whoever falls, guard the swarm
system.description: A dog-sized carrier wasp armored in stolen sheet metal. It hauls loot — and people — back to the nest, and its jaws chew through armor.
While flying, the Arbeiterin has a +1 bonus to her Difficulty. She flies low; a PC can reach her in Melee range from the ground.
When a PC marks an Armor Slot to reduce the Arbeiterin's damage, they must mark an additional Armor Slot.

Mark a Stress to seize a target within Melee range: a PC must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll (14) or be Restrained in her legs. The next time she is spotlighted, she flies up to Far range toward the nest with them. The PC breaks free with a successful Strength Roll or when she takes Major or greater damage.

system.motivesAndTactics: Circle out of reach, mark the haul, call the swarm, wait, never fight alone
system.description: A lone metal wasp circling high above the haze. It marks the haul and counts on a frequency until enough of its kind have answered.
While flying, the Späherin has a +2 bonus to her Difficulty. A PC can only reach her in Melee range by climbing, leaping from something tall, or flying.

Mark a Stress to mark a pile of Scrap, a vehicle, or a PC carrying Scrap within Very Far range, and start a Consequence Countdown (4). It ticks down each time a PC rolls for Scrap or makes an action roll within Far range of the mark. When it triggers, a Wespenschwarm arrives within Close range of the mark and is spotlighted. If the Späherin is defeated before then, the countdown stops.
When the Späherin marks HP, she flies up to Far range away.

system.motivesAndTactics: Guard the hoard, breed the swarm, call every wasp home, let the swarm take the blow
system.description: A metal queen wasp the size of a vehicle, plated in the stolen hoard of her nest. She breeds swarms, holds her people together on one frequency, and lets them die for her.
The Königin can be spotlighted up to two times per GM turn. Spend a Fear as usual to spotlight her.
While the Königin lives, every wasp in the scene knows where every PC is, and swarms don't use Break Off.

While the hoard lies within Close range of her, the Königin has resistance to physical damage. A PC within Melee range of the hoard can make a Strength or Finesse Roll (15) to tear a section away; after two successes, the plating falls and she loses this feature.
Spend a Fear to have a Wespenschwarm hatch from the hoard within Close range. Spotlight it immediately.
When the Königin would take Severe damage and a swarm is within Very Close range, the swarm throws itself in between: it marks 2 HP, and the Königin takes Major damage instead.

5qRxvCIw7fGkfX5N.label: Wespen-Späherin, Wespenschwarm, Wespen-Arbeiterin, Wespenkönigin, Gutters who came for the scrap (Gutter-Crews)

system.description: A wreck the wasps have rebuilt from everything they ever stole — combs of scrap, warm and humming. The richest place in the Deadband, as long as it stays asleep.
system.impulses: Hoard the metal, wake the swarm, hide the queen deep inside

system.description:
The nest is built from stolen Scrap. When the PCs collect Scrap here, each PC rolls one additional Shard and one additional Metal — and each roll ticks down Sleeping Nest.

Whose crew's colors are still on the walls? What did they die for?

When the PCs enter, start a Consequence Countdown (6). It ticks down when a PC rolls for Scrap, makes a loud noise, or fails an action roll. When it triggers, the nest wakes: a Wespenschwarm and a Wespen-Arbeiterin pour out within Close range, and the Königin wakes in her chamber.

What do the PCs hear first — the hum getting louder, or stopping?

The nest hums on one frequency. A PC with a Tuner can make a Knowledge Roll to read it. On a success, they learn how close Sleeping Nest is to triggering and where the queen lies.

What does the hum sound like when it counts down?

Spend a Fear to have a Wespenschwarm pour out of a wall within Close range of a PC. Spotlight it immediately.

Which wall — and what does it drop as it opens?

When a PC tears Scrap out of a wall or the hoard and rolls with Fear, part of the comb gives way. All targets within Very Close range must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (14) or take 2d8 physical damage and be Restrained under the scrap until they dig free with a successful Strength Roll.

What falls out of the wall with the scrap?

system.motivesAndTactics: Swarm the haul, strip the packs, sting the defenders, carry it all home, scatter when many fall
system.description: Hundreds of hand-sized metal wasps that come for the loot, not for the people — and sting anyone who stands in between.
When the swarm has marked half or more of its HP, its standard attack deals 1d4+1 physical damage instead.
While flying, the swarm has a +2 bonus to its Difficulty.

When the swarm succeeds on an attack against a PC who carries Scrap, the PC loses one piece of Scrap of the GM's choice instead of taking damage. A PC who carries none takes damage as normal. The swarm also strips Scrap from open packs and vehicles within Melee range.
When the swarm marks 2 or more HP from a single attack, it flies off up to Very Far range with everything it took and leaves the scene.

The great storm rolls in from the edge on every side at once — a wall of white-gold light shot through with dark violet streaks. Everything the Lumenwerke pumped out comes back, and the Motherboard turns every signal up.
system.impulses: Return what was taken, overwrite every signal, drive the Restlinge mad, bury the unprepared

system.description:
Countdown (8). When the storm arrives, activate the countdown. It ticks down when a PC rolls with Hope. When it triggers, the storm has passed over.

Where is the nearest shelter? What did the PCs leave outside?

The light and the Äther in the air blind everyone. PCs can't see beyond Close range, and they can't move as part of an action roll without succeeding on an Agility Reaction Roll.

What shapes move in the light? Whose voice calls from inside it?

Every signal is loud, and every signal overwrites the others. No technology works in the storm: Funk, Bake and Schirm are dead, an Arx won't fire, Cyware goes silent, and vehicles drop out of the field.

What does the PC hear in the noise? What do they do without the thing they always relied on?

Every Restling in the storm makes all its rolls with advantage.

What was this Restling waiting for? What does the storm tell it?

When the countdown triggers, the storm has torn the dust open. Reveal one thing that wasn't there before: an old cable or pipe no one knew about, a buried machine, or the wreck of someone who didn't reach shelter. Then a player makes a fate roll with their Hope Die: on a 7 or higher, the storm has uncovered old technology the PCs can salvage — roll Scrap as for a standard fight against pure technology (3 Shards · 2 Metals · 2 Components). On a 12, it is something rare: a Steuerkern in Cordex, a Relikt, or something no one has a name for.

Where does the new old line lead? Who else saw it come up?

Spend a Fear to drive a gust of visible Äther through a point within Far range. Each target within Close range of that point must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll or take 4d8+8 magic damage and be thrown up to Far range. Targets who succeed must mark a Stress.

What does the Äther feel like on the skin? What does it tear loose?

Spend a Fear to choose a PC who carries a charged Arx, a Bake or Cyware. The dead device overloads: they must succeed on a Knowledge Reaction Roll or take 4d10+8 magic damage as it burns out. On a success, they tear it loose in time, but it is ruined until repaired.

What smells like burning? What will this repair cost in Rostgrund?

When a PC outside shelter rolls a failure with Fear, a Restling in frenzy appears within Far range of them and immediately takes the spotlight.

What was this Restling built for? Why does it hate them in particular?

system.motivesAndTactics: Drink at the mast, breathe light, crush with claws, retreat to drink again
system.description: A dragon rebuilt in metal by the old world: scales over a tank of Aether, a metal organ in its throat. It drinks at the masts until it glows, then breathes what it has stored.
The Wurm can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend a Fear as usual to spotlight it.
The Wurm starts a scene with 3 tokens on its stat block. While it has no tokens, it is Vulnerable.

Spend a Fear and remove a token to breathe a beam in a line up to Far range. All targets in the line must make an Agility Reaction Roll (17). Targets who fail take 3d12+6 magic damage; targets who succeed take half damage.
While within Very Close range of a Netzpfeiler or a Born, the Wurm restores all its tokens and clears 2 HP.
When the Wurm takes Severe damage while it has tokens, Aether vents from the wound: all targets within Close range must mark a Stress.

system.motivesAndTactics: Drink at the mast, listen, bolt, stampede over whatever is in the way
system.description: A herd of tall, stilt-legged mechanical grazers with tanks of liquid Aether glowing in their flanks. Harmless at the mast — until something startles them.
When the herd has marked half or more of its HP, its standard attack deals 1d6+1 physical damage instead.
The herd ignores the PCs until one of them attacks it, makes a loud noise, or comes within Close range without care.

Mark a Stress: the herd bolts outward in every direction from where it stands. All targets within Close range of the herd must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (11) or take 1d10+3 physical damage and be knocked down, Vulnerable until they next act. A vehicle within Close range is rammed and can't move until someone rights it. Then the herd moves up to Far range away.

When the herd marks HP from an attack within Melee range, a flank window shatters and liquid Aether splashes out. The attacker marks a Stress — unless they catch it with a Leech, in which case they recharge one device or vehicle as if at a mast.
